sources.title: Michael C. A. Macdonald, Arabs, Arabias and Arabic before Late Antiquity (2009)
sources.note: Direct publisher page read, printed p.277, section I: ancient Arab labels have variable criteria. The atlas interval and polygon are independently decoded; regional examples do not establish the self-identification of every inhabitant.

sources.title: Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres, Mission archéologique de Thāj
sources.note: Direct mission account: introductory chronology and debated Gerrha identification; aquifer paragraph; zones 2, 6, 8, 11. Its directional east-of-Jubayl typo is not repeated; Thaj is inland west of the coast. Long-lived wells and fortifications are not dated artificially to one year.

sources.title: Daniel T. Potts, Northeastern Arabia, Expedition (1984)
sources.note: Direct museum article: Gerrha trade, excavation ceramic sequence and Ancient Hasaean Society. Modern Thaj identification remains debated; older linguistic classifications and maximal city-area estimate are not adopted.

sources.title: Polybius, Histories 13.9, W. R. Paton translation
sources.note: Direct primary text 13.9.4 to 5, about Gerrha and Antiochus III; usual 205 BCE date supplied by Potts account. Translated letter is reported by a Greek historian, not a surviving local original.

sources.title: Bruno Overlaet, Wine for the Afterlife: Tombs and Burial Practices at Mleiha in SE-Arabia, volume 65 (2019), 147 to 168
sources.note: Direct institutional repository abstract; indexed original PDF printed p.159 and figure 6 checked with exact title plus "Amud" and "222-221". PDF direct fetch failed. Journal issue is dated 2019; final manuscript approved December 2020. Corrected reading Amud follows Multhoff and Stein 2018. Seleucid-era identification and damaged numeral remain qualified.

sources.title: Global Digital Heritage, Pre-Islamic Mleiha Farmhouse and Kitchen, Sharjah
sources.note: Indexed original documentation PDF, page 1, generated May 19, 2026; description of 2019 scanning. Archaeological phase 200 BCE to 100 CE. Direct PDF extraction failed, original indexed text and creator-linked model description agreed. Distinct from the MLH-04 first-century CE farmhouse discussed by Stein.

sources.title: Peter Stein, South Arabian zabūr script in the Gulf: some recent discoveries from Mleiha (2017)
sources.note: Full publisher text directly read. Introduction: MLH-07 burial chamber dated middle second century BCE. Amphora handle section, figures 9 to 10, transcription and translation; vessel manufacture 225 to 125 BCE. Conclusions distinguish suggested broader writing from absence of recovered everyday correspondence.

sources.title: Wim Van Neer, Wim Wouters and Michel Mouton, Evidence of sun-dried fish at Mleiha (S.-E. Arabia) in antiquity (2013)
sources.note: Full original paper directly read: printed pp.224 to 231. General sequence and earliest occupation p.224; fish across periods p.230; building H final phase, processing and inferred preservation pp.229 to 231. No modern Pakistan pickling procedure is asserted for ancient Arabia.

batchIdentityNotes.scope: Ancient external and internal identities cannot be equated with the imported polygon. Specific eastern and southeastern Arabian sites are contextual examples, not evidence for a pan-Arab state.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Exact published scholarly transcription of a South Arabian cursive ownership inscription, chamber mid-second century BCE. No guessed original glyph rendering or claim of modern Arabic language.
